newsitem.title: USA: CFTC petitioned for electronic cattle exchange.
newsitem.headline: CFTC petitioned for electronic cattle exchange.

text.p: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has received an application from Futurecom, a wholly owned unit of Texas Beef Trading Company, Ltd., for approval of an electronic trading exchange for live cattle and options, a CFTC official said Monday.
CFTC published the application last Friday in the Federal Register and announced a public comment period on the petition until March 3.
Futurecom developer S.H. O'Brien said in a release Monday that, if approved, other designated contracts would be added.

The proposed exchange would match orders electronically. Current bids and offers would be displayed on the user's web browser. Traders would connect to secure servers utilizing user identification and passwords. Any account failing to maintain the necessary margin requirements will be closed immediately after proper notice.

CFTC official Dennis Holden said after the comment period is over, CFTC staff will review the comments and then at some point make a recommendation to the five CFTC commissioners who will vote on whether to approve the application.
